why: THE FRENCH RECORD (Nov 2026, the beginner pass — docs/lang-decks.md "The French beginner pass"). Applied by .claude/decks/french-fix.js after paradigm-fix.js, which stays the record of the folded paradigms. Every meaning here is the English Wiktionary's (kaikki.org extraction, read 2026-11-16, CC BY-SA 4.0) or a moved card's own; every sentence is a Tatoeba sentence named by its French / English ids in the entry's `why` (CC BY 2.0 FR), a Wiktionary usage example, or a moved card's own.

delfa1.why: THE BEGINNER PASS (Nov 2026). 43 inserts take the deck from 433 to 476 notes (29 words that were cards of no French deck, 7 moved from the phrases deck, 7 moved down from A2 and B1); the deck is dealt in the order french-order.json gives; five nouns are shown with the gender the dictionary lists first. The description says all of it: which words were supplied and from where, what the order is, and what the default pace comes to, since a deck cannot set its own daily limit. Its count of cards carrying a pronunciation read 446, the number before paradigm-fix.js folded thirteen notes away; it is set to what is there.

and any of them a lower level already teaches is dropped. 43 MORE WORDS WERE SUPPLIED in November 2026, because a beginner needs them and the page prints none of them: 29 that were cards of no French deck (s'il vous plaît, s'il te plaît, excusez-moi, d'accord, enchanté, à bientôt, il y a, est-ce que, aujourd'hui, fois, the fifteen numbers from treize to mille that were missing, and nord, sud, est and ouest), 7 moved here from the phrases deck (ça va, comment ça va, comment allez-vous, je m'appelle, bonne nuit, bonne journée, à demain) and 7 moved down from A2 and B1 (pouvoir, vouloir, devoir, désolé, parce que, mettre, premier). Their meanings are Wiktionary's and their sentences Tatoeba's, as for every other card. THE ORDER is a teaching order, not a frequency list. First come 86 words chosen by hand: the courtesies (bonjour, au revoir, merci, s'il vous plaît, pardon), the words of a first exchange (je m'appelle, comment allez-vous, ça va, enchanté), the subject pronouns, être and nine more verbs (avoir, il y a, aller, faire, pouvoir, vouloir, parler, habiter, aimer), ne and pas, the question words, zero to ten and the commonest function words. After that the cards follow a frequency list built from film and television subtitles, with each closed set dealt together after the word that introduces it — the days of the week after le jour, the numbers from eleven to a thousand after l'heure, the months after le mois, the seasons after l'année, then the compass points and the colours — and words that are easily confused (l'an and l'année, me and moi) kept forty cards apart. THE PACE: Folio deals ten new cards a day in a language deck unless you change it, and a word is two cards, so this deck is five words a day: the courtesies in the first three days, the 86 chosen words in 18, the whole deck in 96 days. Raise New cards per day in the deck's options to go faster; a deck cannot set that for you. French — Sounds and spelling, the deck before this one on the shelf, says how the letters are read and is meant to be studied beside it.

frphrases.why: THE BEGINNER PASS (Nov 2026). The phrases deck is the last on the shelf, yet 153 of its expressions are spelled entirely with DELF A1's words; it is now dealt by reading level (french-order.json) and its description says it can begin beside A1.
